title: Global Contractor Payments: Payouts API Solutions for On-Demand Manufacturing
summary: Are you struggling to manage tax forms and global contractor payments? Here is how a payouts API simplifies onboarding, compliance, and global payouts.
body_markdown:
**Learn how on-demand manufacturers can onboard, verify, and pay contractors worldwide without the manual paperwork and payment delays.**


On-demand manufacturers rarely rely on one fixed team. A single project might need a mechanical engineer in Poland, a CNC programmer in Mexico, and a quality inspector in Vietnam, all in the same month. The work moves faster, but someone still has to onboard each person, collect the right tax forms, and make sure everyone gets paid on time.


For most finance teams, that someone is already stretched thin. Every new contractor adds another round of emails, spreadsheets, and bank details to double-check.


## Why Global Contractor Payments Get Complicated So Fast


Manufacturers are leaning on flexible talent more than ever. Deloitte's[2026 Manufacturing Industry Outlook](https://www.deloitte.com/us/en/insights/industry/manufacturing-industrial-products/manufacturing-industry-outlook.html) points to a "build, buy or borrow" approach to workforce planning, where borrowed talent covers shifts in demand. A joint study by Deloitte and The Manufacturing Institute,[summarized by Plastics Today](https://www.plasticstoday.com/industry-trends/talent-talk-manufacturing-faces-critical-worker-shortage-in-coming-decade) , estimates the industry needs 3.8 million new workers over the next decade, and that half of those roles could go unfilled. Contractors fill that gap, and many of them live abroad.


Each one brings paperwork. Foreign individuals generally certify their status on[IRS Form W-8BEN](https://www.irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-w-8-ben) , while US-based contractors submit a W-9. Mistakes are costly, since the IRS charges[penalties for incorrect or late information returns](https://www.irs.gov/payments/information-return-penalties) . Add identity checks, currency conversion, and bank formats that change from country to country, and a simple payment becomes a multi-day task.


## What is a Payouts API and How Does It Simplify Contractor Payments?


A[payouts API](https://usedots.com/platform/payouts-api/) is a connection between your own systems and a payment network. Instead of logging into a bank portal and keying in details by hand, your software sends a payment instruction, and the platform handles the rest.


The better versions go beyond moving money. They collect[tax forms](https://usedots.com/platform/tax/) , verify identities, check recipient details, and route each payment through the best available route for that country. For a finance team, that means one workflow in place of five separate tools and a shared folder full of PDFs.


## How Do You Pay International Contractors Without Manual Wire Transfers?


Traditional wires work, but they were not built for a steady stream of small, global payments. Here is how the two approaches compare in practice:


- **Manual wire transfers:** Someone enters bank details for every payment, fees stack up through intermediary banks, and funds can take several days to land. A single typo can send a payment back.
- **An automated payouts API:** Payment details are captured once during onboarding, payments can be scheduled or triggered from your project system, and funds arrive in the contractor's local currency through local payment methods.


The time savings matter as much as the fee savings. When payments run automatically, your team stops answering where is my money? emails and gets back to work that actually moves the business forward.


## Do You Need Tax Forms for Foreign Contractors?


In most cases, yes. A W-8 form documents that a contractor is not a US taxpayer, and it protects your business if the IRS ever asks why you did not withhold or report on a payment. Collecting these forms by email is where things usually slip. Forms arrive incomplete, expire, or never arrive at all.


A[payouts API](https://usedots.com/platform/payouts/) builds the request into onboarding. The contractor completes the correct form before the first payment, the platform stores it, and the right 1099 reporting is handled at year end. Nothing depends on someone remembering to follow up.


## Can Identity Verification and Background Checks Happen Before Payment?


They can, and it is a smart place to catch problems early. Manufacturers often give contractors access to designs, specifications, and production data, so confirming who they are before the first payment protects more than your books.


When identity verification sits inside the same flow as onboarding and payouts, a contractor can go from invitation to approved payee without a separate vendor. It also leaves a clear record, which makes audits far less painful.
